messages:
julia: Quick sync — we need to triage the Optimize toolkit RFC items for Q2 planning: batching heuristics, prefix/KV caching, and quantization recommendation flow. Customer asks from Acme (cost-focused hosted) and FinCorp (on-prem latency guarantees). I want a short PRD + acceptance criteria and a proposed launch checklist by EOD Wednesday. Thoughts?

anil: +1. I'll draft technical acceptance criteria. Quick callouts: batching should not increase p99 by >10% for short queries, caching must have TTL and eviction policy, quantization must include fallback to fp16 for regressions.

maria: For quantization, we need objective quality checks per model: BLEU/ROUGE for seq tasks and embedding cosine drop < 0.02 on our eval sets. Also add synthetic adversarial prompts to catch hallucination shifts.

sam: From infra side: rollout needs feature-flagged canary, dark-launch for 2% traffic, and ability to route specific customers (FinCorp) to non-quantized path. We'll need dashboards: token-cost-per-request, batch-size distribution, cache hit ratio, and p50/p95/p99 latencies.

leo: Prioritization note: Acme wants cost wins ASAP — batching + cache could give them ~30% token cost reduction. FinCorp will only accept if p99 < 250ms on their on-prem instance; quantization is lower priority for them. Recommend splitting into two tracks: "cost-first" (batching+cache) and "LLM-ops" (quantization, eval infra).

julia: Good split. For the PRD I'm thinking small, measurable milestones: M1 = internal alpha with API knobs + basic metrics; M2 = customer pilot (Acme); M3 = GA with docs + guided migration. Acceptance criteria ideas?

anil: Draft acceptance criteria quick list:
- Batching: mean throughput increase >= 25% for steady-state workloads; median latency change <= 5%; p99 latency delta <= +10%.
- Cache: end-to-end cache hit ratio >= 40% on repeat-heavy workloads; cache TTL configurable per route; correctness: cached outputs must be verbatim only for deterministic routes.
- Quantization: model size reduction >= 2x (vs fp16) for 8-bit configs; quality regression <= 1% on primary eval suites; automatic fallback to higher-precision if confidence metric falls below threshold.

maria: Edge cases we should call out in PRD:
- Non-deterministic ops (sampling temperature >0) should not use prefix cache unless request includes a `deterministic: true` flag.
- Long-running streams: batching should short-circuit for streaming requests to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Mixed-precision KV cache consistency if model architecture changes between versions.

sam: Ops checklist items for launch:
1) Canary routing + feature flags implemented.
2) Metrics + alerts: cost-per-token delta, cache hit < 20% alert, p99 latency > SLO.
3) Run a simulated workload replay for Acme and FinCorp hardware profiles.
4) Backout plan docs + automated revert playbook.

julia: Nice. We also need acceptance criteria that are customer-facing so sales/solutions can promise something. Proposed customer-facing SLA bullets: token cost reduction target (best-effort), configurable latency SLOs for Dedicated/Private, and quality guardrails with rollback.

leo: For sales: we'll need a migration guide and a checklist for when to enable `quant=8bit` vs keep `fp16`. Suggest rule-of-thumb: enable quantization for prompt-only flows and embedding workloads after internal eval.

anil: Quick config snippet for the rollout plan to include in RFC:
```yaml
service: optimize-toolkit
routes:
  - name: default
    batching: true
    cache:
      enabled: true
      ttl: 300
    quantization:
      default: auto
      allowed_modes: [fp16, int8]
    rollout:
      canary_percent: 2
      feature_flag: enable_optimize_v1
```

maria: Tests we need to add to eval harness:
- Regression suite (1000 prompts) run across all candidate quant modes.
- Cache correctness fuzzer (randomized prompt sequences).
- Batching stress tests with mixed sequence lengths.

julia: Who owns the PRD and the initial RFC writeup? I'll own the customer-facing PRD. @anil own the RFC with technical acceptance criteria and perf tests. Maria, own eval harness additions. Sam, ops/runbook + dashboards. Leo, compile sales assets. Deadline: draft PRD + RFC by EOD Wednesday, short review on Thursday.

leo: Ack. I'll prepare a one-pager for sales that lists tradeoffs and suggested messaging.

anil: I'll post a small perf plan tomorrow: what benchmarks, data collection, and expected run time. Also note: we should include a controlled A/B that compares cost/latency/quality across the two tracks.

maria: I'll add a note about version pinning: quantized weights must be pinned per model version to avoid silent diffs. Also add a model-signature check at load time.

sam: Ops-bot: link to canary rollout checklist?

ops-bot: Canary checklist created: https://internal.redwood/canary-checklists/optimize-toolkit-v1 — items 1-12. :white_check_mark:

julia: Great. Last Q: do we want to include adaptive batching recommendations in the same RFC or a follow-up? Adaptive batching touches runtime scheduling; I think include a minimal heuristic (max wait 25ms, max batch size 32) and move tuning to follow-up RFC. Decision?

anil: Agree. Minimal heuristics in initial RFC, detailed scheduler changes as follow-up RFC.

julia: Perfect. I'll start the PRD draft now and ping reviewers when ready. Thanks all. :rocket:
